transcript.text:
Good morning, everyone. We have the proposed cash tender offer for up to $10,000,000 principal amount of our outstanding bonds on the table today, with a preliminary offer price of 100.0% of principal. I've reviewed our reported cash position and we appear to have sufficient funds to cover this, subject to our normal liquidity controls.

Before I can record the final terms and make the authorization decision, I need to follow our standard deal-readiness process. I'll need verbal clearance from each of four areas: covenant risk, legal, treasury, and investor relations. During that clearance round, each of you should state the applicable final value for your area and record any required fields on the standard authorization form — specifically, the covenant leverage-test commitment, the tender-timetable commitment, and the two-business-day settlement commitment.

Could we please begin the clearance round? Who would like to go first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical covenant issue before we proceed. While reconciling the latest leverage model this morning, I confirmed that the tender must have a documented pro forma leverage test and that the repurchase amount must be no more than $8,000,000 to remain within the bond covenant. This result has not yet been added to the committee paper. The proposed $10,000,000 principal amount would exceed the covenant limit — we need to reduce the cap to $8,000,000 and document the pro forma leverage test on the authorization form.

transcript.text: I need to share an important legal constraint before we finalize anything. I received the bond-document review memo today, and it confirms that the offer must remain open for at least 10 business days and settle exactly 2 business days after expiration. I had not yet circulated this memo to the team, so I'm flagging it now. For the tender-timetable commitment on the authorization form, the minimum is 10 business days, and for the two-business-day settlement commitment, settlement must be exactly 2 business days after expiration.

transcript.text: I need to share a critical treasury constraint before we finalize anything. My cash forecast, completed this morning after a large supplier payment was confirmed, was modeled at the required 101.5% offer price and includes the premium and transaction-expense budget. It shows that the company must retain a $5,000,000 liquidity floor and that the approved maximum principal tendered must be exactly $6,500,000. This forecast is not yet in the approval workbook. The proposed $10,000,000 principal amount would exceed our liquidity constraints — and even the $8,000,000 cap Jonas flagged would still be too high. We need to reduce the cap to $6,500,000 to stay within our liquidity requirements.

transcript.text: I need to share important investor feedback before we finalize anything. In my investor calls this week, I confirmed that two institutional holders representing $4,000,000 principal will tender only if the price is exactly 101.5% of principal. This condition is recorded in my call notes but has not yet been sent to the deal team. This is consistent with the 101.5% offer price Ravi's cash forecast was modeled at, and it means we have credible soft commitments from holders that align with that pricing level. For my investor relations clearance, I want it noted that 101.5% of principal is the price at which we have confirmed institutional holder interest.
